key_insight: Delta-VQE can detect phase boundaries with shallow variational circuits, but only when the ansatz is physically aligned with the competing phases; otherwise it may falsely lock onto self-dual points.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a resource-efficient way to probe quantum criticality on near-term hardware, while emphasizing that ansatz design is as important as circuit depth for reliable phase detection.
method: Use VQE energies from two reference ansätze associated with different phases.
Compare optimized variational energies to locate where the phase preference switches.
Tested on the 1D transverse-field Ising model with three-spin cluster interaction.
evidence_signal: In the studied model, dual ansätze consistently flagged self-dual points instead of the true critical points, whereas carefully phase-matched ansätze recovered the genuine Ising transition with only small finite-size effects.
watch_item: The method is highly ansatz-dependent, so poorly chosen reference circuits can produce systematic false positives even when the variational optimization is working correctly.
paper_title: Detecting quantum phase transitions via shallow variational quantum circuits
